CNA VulnCheck describes GraphQL connection-level helpers.request failure re-thrown unchanged; the client error retains live request headers including a decrypted credential secret, which the execution engine persists; an authenticated execution reader can recover it. CWE-209.

Vendor repository advisory https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/security/advisories/GHSA-9fqj-7wc5-cwhx is state published, withdrawn_at null, closed_at null. Same source-to-sink. GitHub Advisory Database GHSA-8329-w544-9mx3 aliases CVE-2026-77076, withdrawn_at null, and points at the vendor advisory; GitHub withdrawn_at is not treated as authoritative.

On affected tags n8n@1.123.68 (67e50ebb0689dd587704aa533f35f51839f860f9), n8n@2.33.3 (12d3f08599176aeecd04c63f23ae7d4e0f4874e9), and n8n@2.34.0 (b533ecd6856fef9ba7ca096d14b1f798b9933ff6), GraphQL.node.ts copies httpHeaderAuth.value into requestOptions.headers and on helpers.request rejection executes raw `throw error` (lines 582 / 588 / 588). GraphQL response.errors are already NodeApiError-wrapped; the leak is the connection-error path.

Direct-fix test added with ca3d42d8386515cd9f044377a15a632cd09b62f0 builds an axios-style request error whose options.headers.Authorization is `credential-value` and asserts the resulting NodeApiError has no options property and JSON.stringify omits that secret. NodeApiError constructs a new n8n error from selected message/status fields and does not copy request options.

GitHub PR https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/pull/1805 reports commits=1, head 0dc28e4e813defaa0c16004c3cb72f30e52b0eba, merge_commit_sha d3aa637ff4e634abad08150a27e9d2fce7d8fa07. The /pulls/1805/commits API returns only 0dc28e4e813defaa0c16004c3cb72f30e52b0eba.

That one-file commit (packages/nodes-base/nodes/GraphQL/GraphQL.node.ts, +36) is the first public writer of the decrypted-credential source: it declares credentials httpHeaderAuth, calls this.getCredentials('httpHeaderAuth'), and assigns httpHeaderAuth.value onto requestOptions.headers immediately before helpers.request(requestOptions). Parent already lets the helpers.request rejection escape unwrapped, so source and sink are jointly present for the first time here.

d6239d5bfbc1d701c7a3bebc2c59e1f23ef6aebb later wraps the same execute body in try/catch and `throw error` when !continueOnFail(); it does not add credentials. Subsequent GraphQL error-handling commits (8a94f1e361fa9bd464d01445d3d3a9c3349c6827, e8937aaa21299f757b48c141be2809f6c20a40c3) wrap GraphQL response.errors, not the connection-level client error. No later unwrap re-opens a previously closed leak.
